summary:
Held 3 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 3 upside misses — CRWD +12%, CVNA +8%, MPWR +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (IBM -25%, BIIB -8%, NOW -6%, GEHC -6%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: IBM (-24.54%) — Pre-market CEO letter flagged prelim Q2 revenue of $17.2B (vs $17.86B est.); mainframe/infrastructure weakness as clients redirected capex to AI hardware. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe (mega-cap legacy tech/enterprise IT, not in tradable list). Even if included, the gap was driven by a pre-market CEO disclosure hours before open, so post-open momentum/mean-reversion signals had no edge — price had already re-rated by the bell.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide cyber rally after IBM's Q2 warning flagged spending shifting to cybersecurity, plus cooler June CPI boosting growth names; CRWD hit a 52-wk high on Benchmark/UBS target hikes.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely — likely excluded as a single-name cybersecurity/software growth stock rather than an index/mega-cap constituent, and its July 2 4-for-1 split may have reset volume/price history screens.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-agnostic 'peer-group sympathy' rule: when 2+ names in the same GICS sub-industry (e.g. cybersecurity: FTNT, PANW) gap >5% on a common macro catalyst, auto-admit correlated large-caps into the momentum universe for that session.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 EPS $20.98 vs $14.40 est, revenue +39% YoY to $20.34B on record equity underwriting (+130%) amid AI-driven dealmaking boom
top_movers.miss_reason: GS sits outside any active strategy's universe (large-cap financials/banks category not covered by the currently-live momentum/mean-reversion/news-reactive strategies), so no filter ever evaluated the post-earnings gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap financials (GS, MS, JPM) to news-reactive-disclosure's universe with an earnings-gate rule releasing names on post-results gap ≥5% within 30 min of open.

top_movers.catalyst: CVNA confirmed Q2 earnings (July 29) with CFO reiterating guidance for all-time-record retail units & EBITDA, amplified by peer KMX's strong beat/turnaround lifting used-car retail sentiment.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe entirely - CVNA is likely excluded as a high-beta, historically volatile/meme-prone auto-retail name that momentum/mean-reversion filters screen out on volatility or sector-classification grounds, not by market cap.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a pre-earnings-date-confirmation trigger: when a name announces its earnings date with reiterated beat-and-raise guidance, add it to a 2-week watchlist universe so gap-anticipation moves aren't missed entirely.

top_movers.catalyst: Wave of same-day analyst price-target hikes (Evercore/Goldman/Morgan Stanley to $500/$477) on AI-server demand optimism, plus a political tailwind from Michael Dell's $6B Trump Accounts pledge highlighted at an Oval Office event.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DELL is classified as legacy PC/hardware OEM rather than AI-semis/software momentum, so static universes never included it; only regime-router's opportunistic, non-universe-gated logic could reach it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap AI-server-exposed hardware OEMs (DELL, HPE, SMCI) to the momentum-trader universe, or let regime-router's dynamic picks auto-promote a name into other strategies' universes after 2+ same-day analyst target hikes.

top_movers.catalyst: IBM's Q2 profit warning/miss ($17.2B rev vs $17.9B est) and CEO comments on cybersecurity budget resilience sparked a sector-wide rally; PANW closed +6.8% to $352.89.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — PANW is a large-cap cybersecurity software name, but the move was peer-contagion from IBM's earnings miss on a different ticker, not a PANW-specific signal a name-scoped scanner would catch.
top_movers.suggestion: Add PANW/CRWD/OKTA/ZS/S to a large-cap cybersecurity universe bucket, and add a peer-contagion trigger that flags sector peers for review when one constituent (e.g. IBM) posts an outsized earnings surprise.

top_movers.catalyst: Broad semiconductor/AI-infra rally (soft CPI print + IBM capex read-through) plus MPWR reaffirming its $2.00/share Q2 dividend ahead of July 30 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — MPWR is a ~$1,378/share large-cap semiconductor name likely excluded by a share-price or notional-per-position cap rather than by sector/liquidity screens.
top_movers.suggestion: Switch universe inclusion and position sizing from share-count-based to notional/dollar-based limits (or allow fractional shares) so high-priced names like MPWR aren't filtered out purely on price-per-share.

top_movers.catalyst: Pre-market CEO letter flagged prelim Q2 revenue of $17.2B (vs $17.86B est.); mainframe/infrastructure weakness as clients redirected capex to AI hardware.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mega-cap legacy tech/enterprise IT, not in tradable list). Even if included, the gap was driven by a pre-market CEO disclosure hours before open, so post-open momentum/mean-reversion signals had no edge — price had already re-rated by the bell.
top_movers.suggestion: If adding IBM-class large-cap tech to universe, pair with an overnight-gap news gate that flags pre-market CEO/8-K disclosures and either holds new entries for T+1 confirmation or explicitly excludes same-day entry on gaps >10%.

top_movers.catalyst: Phase II CELIA data for Alzheimer's candidate diranersen missed its primary dose-response endpoint (lowest dose beat higher doses), reviving doubts about the late-stage program.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BIIB is a large-cap biotech whose moves are binary/trial-readout-driven, a profile momentum and mean-reversion equity strategies typically exclude given event-risk and gap unpredictability.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a narrow biotech-catalyst watchlist (conference/PDUFA calendar-gated) so large-cap names with scheduled trial readouts get temporary universe inclusion around known event dates.

top_movers.catalyst: Fell in sympathy with IBM's disappointing preliminary Q2 results, given their close enterprise-AI partnership; NOW reports its own Q2 on 7/22.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (large-cap enterprise SaaS, not covered) — but even if tracked, this was a peer-contagion/read-through move on IBM's print, not NOW's own news, which pre-market/relative-strength signals on IBM would need to catch, not NOW's own price action.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a peer-contagion trigger: when a closely-partnered/comped name (e.g., IBM) reports a pre-market miss, flag correlated large-cap peers (NOW) for a same-day review even if outside the core universe.

top_movers.catalyst: HCA's Q2 warning (weaker surgery volumes, unfavorable payer mix) sparked read-through selling in medtech suppliers, amplifying fears from GEHC's own soft Q1 order growth (1.1% vs 10.3% y/y).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — GEHC is a large-cap medtech/imaging-equipment name, likely excluded because current universes are scoped to core sector ETFs/names rather than hospital-equipment suppliers reacting to peer (HCA) guidance.
top_movers.suggestion: Add GEHC to the universe of any large-cap healthcare-equipment strategy, and add a peer-read-through rule flagging equipment suppliers when a major hospital operator (e.g., HCA) issues a volume/payer-mix warning intraday.
